title: Production ClayCode package-lock/provenance differential on Ubuntu
goal: Attempt the candidate typed package-lock/provenance contract in the production current ClayCode toolchain and falsify identity-plane assumptions before BASE promotion.
required_tests: Generate a lock from a version-range package request, then grow registry state: unlocked resolution may change; locked/frozen execution must not silently drift.
Mutate package payload under the same logical coordinate/version in a controlled local registry fixture: digest verification must fail closed.
Permute package/node/edge discovery order: canonical ResolvedGraphId and BuildProjectionId must remain stable.
Fetch identical verified logical package coordinate/content through two different mirrors: semantic graph/projection identity should remain stable while FetchReceipt differs.
Resolve same name/version/content under a deliberately distinct logical source namespace/authority: test whether PackageCoordinate/ResolvedGraphId changes as designed.
Change Ubuntu target/features/semantic markers so active dependency meaning changes: BuildProjectionId must change while underlying ResolvedGraphId may remain stable.

Apply yank/revocation/freshness policy after graph identification: immutable graph identity must remain stable while SupplyChainTrustReceipt verdict changes and use is blocked where policy says REJECT.
Run two resolver implementations/policies against a fixture that yields the same exact graph: ResolvedGraphId should match and ResolutionReceipt should differ.
Package declares a network/system effect without external capability grant: execution must be denied; explicit grant should permit only the granted authority.
Exercise candidate semantic cache: compare full rebuild vs cache reuse under trust-only changes and under actual semantic BuildProjection changes; no stale semantic artifact reuse is allowed.
required_receipts: resolver policy/version and registry input hashes
language_change_rule: Only EXECUTABLE_LANGUAGE_SEMANTIC_COUNTEREXAMPLE may justify reopening ClayCode core semantics; otherwise repair compiler/runtime/package/toolchain layers.
